Use case: sketch-to-render.
Asset type: industrial modular spacecraft KIT OVERVIEW based exactly on the user's graybox.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and authoritative layout/shape reference: the user's graybox overview. Input image 2 is supporting reference showing how six of those same parts assemble.
Make a realistic material/lighting concept sheet of precisely the SAME TWELVE distinct parts from input 1, in the SAME TWO ROWS of SIX and the same viewing directions. Retain relative scale across parts: do not enlarge a small module to fill a cell.
Top row left to right: 1) HULL 1x1x1, a small cube; 2) HULL 2x2x1, a broad shallow square body; 3) HULL 2x4x1, twice as long with the same width/height; 4) CORRIDOR 2x1x1, a narrow horizontal tube with square end collars; 5) COCKPIT 2x2x1, the same low wedge cockpit with dark canopy; 6) CARGO 2x2x1, a shallow square cargo body with transverse ribs.
Bottom row left to right: 7) REACTOR 2x2x1, a shallow square base with one small central cylindrical cap and four corner posts; 8) ENGINE L 2x2x2, one large bell nozzle pointing left and square mounting plate on the right; 9) THRUSTER 1x1x1, smaller bell nozzle pointing left, square mount on right; 10) TURRET 1x1x1, a compact twin-barrel gun on a traverse base, barrels pointing right; 11) SOLAR 1x1x1, one single flat rectangular panel on a short bracket; 12) DOCK 1x1x1, a short horizontal tube between two end flanges.
This list comes from the actual .blend file. It supersedes any previous kit images: do NOT insert a separate small engine, remove the 1x1 hull, replace the round dock tube with a giant square door, invent extra parts, or redesign the kit into little whole spaceships.
STRICT shape lock: preserve low hull height, long 2x4 proportions, connector marker locations and counts, the single solar panel rectangle, compact weapons and bell engines. The yellow squares are mechanical interface markers to restyle, NOT toy yellow tiles.
The user's material and lighting requirements are authoritative:
Materials: brushed steel, matte painted armor plates, scratches, localized oil stains, black rubber seals; emissive strips ONLY at connection ports.
Lighting: one strong dominant key light, secondary rim light, deep contrast, grounded ambient occlusion, subtle volumetric dust.
Palette: desaturated dark gunmetal, one restrained accent color per module TYPE, very limited neon.
Proportions: heavy industrial, precise narrow chamfered edges, mechanical realism, no rounded toy shapes.
Atmospheric design references: Dead Space, Alien Isolation, Starfield, Elite Dangerous, The Expanse. Use their grounded manufactured industrial science-fiction qualities, without copying recognizable ships, logos or characters.
Use physically convincing material response: directional brushed steel revealed on machined edges, dry matte paint on large armor plates, fine scratches concentrated near servicing areas and corners, sparse oily streaks around joints, rubber gaskets around mechanical interfaces. Broad plate planes, modest panel divisions, credible material thickness, no random greeble carpet.
IMPORTANT: the graybox's large YELLOW SQUARES are connection location markers, NOT yellow decorations to retain. Turn each marker into a dark square mechanical interface plate of the same size and position, with recessed socket, metal latch details and a rubber perimeter seal. Tiny local indicator strips may appear only INSIDE the connector rims. NO glowing hull seams, roof rails, windows, gun barrels, solar panel edges, or continuous neon trims.
Type colors: structural/engine/dock interfaces use restrained amber; reactor interfaces use muted cyan; weapon interface uses muted oxide orange-red; cockpit/corridor use a subdued warm-white interface indicator; cargo uses muted ochre. Treat solar cells as almost-black blue technical material, not an extra neon accent. Each type uses one accent only; accents occupy under 3 percent of visible area. Most of the image is neutral metal and matte dark paint. No giant yellow borders.
Preserve the graybox's body dimensions and planar proportions. Narrow mechanical chamfers, not inflated rounded bevels. No chibi, miniature-toy, mobile-cartoon, glossy plastic or stylized outlines. This should look like a full-scale manufactured industrial vehicle, rendered with high-end realistic game-asset materials.
Presentation: an orderly two-row industrial asset catalog on a neutral medium-dark charcoal backdrop, almost orthographic elevated front view matching input 1. Bring the objects closer within the same grid arrangement to use the frame efficiently, but never change their relative scale. All parts completely visible with clear empty gaps; no overlapping labels.
Use one restrained small off-white technical caption BELOW each module, exactly:
"HULL 1x1x1", "HULL 2x2x1", "HULL 2x4x1", "CORRIDOR", "COCKPIT", "CARGO";
"REACTOR", "ENGINE L", "THRUSTER", "TURRET", "SOLAR", "DOCK".
No title, no logos, no extra typography. The key light is consistent across all 12 parts, with deep occlusion at joints, restrained rim separation, and barely visible background dust. Keep small parts legible through controlled lighting without making the style cartoonish.
Maximum available native resolution. This is an art direction render, not a new design of the graybox.
